summary: Unexpected tenant quota exhaustion and 429s traced to internal health-check probes
description: Issue summary: BrightCart reports repeated 429 responses for production API keys across a dedicated pool beginning 2026-03-09 22:15 UTC. Impact: customer-facing inference endpoints return 429s for short bursts causing failed user requests and follow-up retries. Environment: Dedicated capacity (BrightCart dedicated pool) in us-east-1. Key observation: total token/requests quota for the tenant appeared to be depleted at times when customer traffic was low. Suspected cause: internal health-checks or probes consuming quota unexpectedly.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy app using BrightCart's production API key against Redwood hosted endpoint in us-east-1.
2) Wait for scheduled health-check window between 22:00-23:00 UTC (customer's LB warmup).
3) Observe numerous short requests from the same API key without proper session pinning.
4) Observe 429 responses returned by Redwood within 5-10 minute windows and quota counters decreasing in Console usage pane.

2026-03-09T22:19:00Z billing usage-report tenant=brightcart tokens=12543 source=api-key-brc-prod-01 note=high-frequency-200ms-probes
Edge proxy logs: multiple 40-60ms small requests from 52.14.23.0/24 labeled 'health-check' using same API key.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 Support (Aisha): Customer noticed intermittent 429s starting 2026-03-09 22:15 UTC. Provided token usage screenshot and sample request IDs. Asked for rate-limit counters and recent quota activity.

2026-03-10 10:05 SRE (Marcus): Confirmed tenant token exhaustion windows align with cluster health-check schedule. Spun up quick sampling of logs and flagged high-frequency probes using customer's prod key.
2026-03-10 11:30 Customer (BrightCart - Omar): We run an autoscaling LB with health-checks every 10s during warmups. We did not expect those probes to count against API quota. Please advise.

2026-03-11 08:48 Support (Aisha): Reproduced in staging by running 8s interval health checks against staging key; observed equivalent quota drawdown. Raised INT ticket to engineering for policy review.

2026-03-12 14:22 SRE (Marcus): Implemented temporary mitigation on gateway to ignore requests with header X-Health-Check: 1 for quota accounting for dedicated pools; scheduled follow-up to formalize exemption rules.
investigation_notes: Initial anomaly: quota counters dropped by ~12k tokens within 10 minutes while customer reported low application traffic. Correlated timestamps with our edge-proxy and dedicated-pool LB logs; found ~600 small probe requests per minute from customer's load balancer IP range. These probes used the customer's production API key (automatically set in their LB config). Confirmed that current quota accounting is per-request and does not exclude perceived health-checks. Risk: if customers configure LB health-checks with production keys or short intervals, they may unknowingly consume quota and hit 429s.
workaround: Advise customer to: 1) rotate the prod API key and create a separate low-privilege key or internal-only key for health checks; 2) temporarily increase dedicated quota commit with account manager if needed; 3) adjust LB probe interval to >=30s until a permanent policy is in place.
resolution: Temporary mitigation applied: gateway will treat requests carrying header 'X-Health-Check: 1' from known customer LB IP ranges as out-of-band for quota accounting for BrightCart's dedicated pool. This was rolled out only to the BrightCart routing rule to avoid cross-tenant risk. Engineering to implement a configurable health-check exemption whitelist in the rate-limiter for dedicated pools. Customer informed and accepted workaround. No further 429s observed in the monitored window after mitigation.
follow_up_actions: 1) Engineering: implement controlled health-check exemption feature in rate-limiter (INT-9821).
2) Product: document recommended health-check key patterns and guidance in Dev Center runbook.
3) Support: notify other dedicated tenants via customer bulletin about best practices for LB health checks and API keys.
4) Security: review whitelist risk and approve RBAC for health-check keys.
5) Billing: verify usage adjustments and issue credit if any overage occurred during the incident window.
